title: Small diagrams of module sheaves form a Grothendieck category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site (small in a universe containing the values of all sheaves), let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings, not necessarily commutative, and let $J$ be a small category in that universe. Let $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ denote the category of sheaves of left $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The category $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\Mod(\mathcal O))$, whose objects are functors and whose maps are natural transformations, is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it is abelian, has all small colimits, its filtered colimits are exact, and it has a generator.

source.place: Tag 05AB (section-grothendieck-categories); Tag 079A (section-grothendieck-conditions) for AB5 and generator; Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D) for the ringed-site example. Agent extension to small diagrams, not a theorem asserted verbatim by these tags.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]: the site and the ring values are small in the specified universe, and this theorem uses left modules over arbitrary rings. Thus $\mathcal A$ is abelian, has all small colimits and exact filtered colimits, and admits a generator $G$ detecting distinct parallel maps.

source.place: Tag 079B (definition-grothendieck-conditions); Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), ringed-site example. Agent extension to small diagrams, with explicit Mathlib ingredients cited as nodes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-functor-abelian-colimits] with this $\mathcal A$ and the given small $J$. It supplies abelianness and all small colimits in $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal A)$. In particular the coproducts used below exist.

source.place: Tag 079B (definition-grothendieck-conditions); Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), ringed-site example. Agent extension to small diagrams, with explicit Mathlib ingredients cited as nodes.

proof.text: For each small filtered category $I$, the exact filtered colimits supplied in step 1 are colimits preserving finite limits. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-functor-exact-colimits] to this $I$ and $J$. The finite-limit hypothesis holds because $\mathcal A$ is abelian. Consequently $\mathcal D$ has exact $I$-colimits, for every such $I$, hence exact filtered colimits.

source.place: Tag 079B (definition-grothendieck-conditions); Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), ringed-site example. Agent extension to small diagrams, with explicit Mathlib ingredients cited as nodes.

proof.text: For each object $j$ of $J$, form $L_j(G)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-evaluation-free-diagram-adjunction]. All indexing sets $\operatorname{Hom}_J(j,k)$ are small and $\mathcal A$ has the required coproducts. Define $H=\coprod_{j\in\operatorname{Ob}J}L_j(G)$ in $\mathcal D$; this is a small coproduct by smallness of $J$ and step 2.

source.place: Tag 079B (definition-grothendieck-conditions); Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), ringed-site example. Agent extension to small diagrams, with explicit Mathlib ingredients cited as nodes.

proof.text: To prove that $H$ is a generator, let $f,g:F\to F'$ be distinct natural transformations. Some $j$ has $f_j\ne g_j$. By the generator property of $G$, choose $h:G\to F(j)$ with $f_j\circ h\ne g_j\circ h$. The adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-evaluation-free-diagram-adjunction] sends $h$ to $a:L_j(G)\to F$; naturality in the target shows that $f\circ a$ and $g\circ a$ correspond to those two distinct maps and are therefore distinct. The coproduct universal property gives $b:H\to F$ restricting to $a$ on the $j$ summand and to zero on every other summand. If $f\circ b=g\circ b$, precomposing with the $j$ coproduct injection would give $f\circ a=g\circ a$, a contradiction. Thus $H$ detects distinct parallel maps. If $J$ is empty, its functor category has exactly one morphism between any pair of objects, so the empty coproduct is a generator vacuously.

source.place: Tag 079B (definition-grothendieck-conditions); Tag 079Q (remark-existence-D), ringed-site example. Agent extension to small diagrams, with explicit Mathlib ingredients cited as nodes.

proof.text: We have proved that $\mathcal D$ is abelian, has all small colimits and exact filtered colimits, and has a generator $H$. These are exactly the requirements of [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], so $\mathcal D$ is Grothendieck abelian.
